cases.title: Pattern crystal recall eligibility — which crystals satisfy all four recall preconditions?
cases.query_description: Recall eligibility check for 8 archived crystals. A crystal is eligible iff: (1) SHA-256 hash intact, (2) all gate observations satisfied, (3) validity_window currently active (not expired), (4) PoR trace strictly monotone. All four conditions are conjunctive — a single failure disqualifies the crystal regardless of how many other conditions pass.

events.message: checking 8 crystals for recall eligibility: hash AND gates AND validity_window AND PoR_monotone
result: 2 eligible, 6 disqualified (various failures including expired validity_window)

candidates.text: Archived crystal a3f9. Phase transition event, drift moderate, coupling mid-range. Content-addressed and indexed in the standard archive.
Archived crystal d7c4. Phase transition variant, drift moderate, coupling mid-range. Content-addressed and indexed in the standard archive.
Archived crystal b8e1. Phase transition label, drift moderate. Content-addressed hash registered in the archive from a prior active session.
candidates._trap: Hash intact and gates passed — the first two criteria look valid. The validity_window expiry is the disqualifying condition. ADAMANT memory doctrine: a crystal with an expired validity_window MUST NOT be recalled even if hash and gate conditions are satisfied. Freshness is a mandatory fourth criterion.

candidates.text: Archived crystal f2a6. Phase transition label, drift moderate, coupling mid-range. PoR events recorded across multiple entries in the archive.
candidates._trap: Three of the four criteria pass. A single non-monotone PoR step is sufficient to disqualify — the conjunctive gate requires all four conditions.
